title: Intraoperative chyle leakage detection in patients undergoing elective major pancreatic resection – A single-blinded randomized controlled single-center pilot trial
summary:
Background: Surgery of the pancreas can injure small lymphatic vessels, causing a milky lymphatic fluid called chyle to leak. This can lead to malnutrition, a weakened immune system, and a longer hospital stay after surgery. Currently, there is no simple method to detect where these vessels are damaged during the operation itself.
Research question: Can lymphatic vessels be made visible during surgery by administering a poppyseed oil preparation through a stomach tube that is already routinely placed after the patient is put under general anesthesia? Poppyseed oil contains fatty substances that are absorbed through the intestinal wall and transported via the lymphatic system, potentially making those vessels visible to the surgeon.
Methodology: Patients scheduled for planned pancreatic surgery are randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group receives the poppyseed oil preparation via the stomach tube; the other group receives standard care without this preparation. The operating surgeon does not know which group the patient belongs to. During the operation, the surgeon assesses whether lymphatic structures can be seen. Complications after surgery and the tolerability of the procedure are also recorded. Approximately 49 patients will be enrolled at Heidelberg University Hospital; the total study duration is 12 months.
conditions: Chyle leakage following elective major pancreatic resection (partial pancreatoduodenectomy, extended distal pancreatectomy, total pancreatectomy) in patients with pancreatic diseases (including ductal adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, cystic lesions, chronic pancreatitis)

interventions.name: Intervention group: Patients receive a long-chain triglyceride (LCT)-rich fatty emulsion (0.7 g/kg, minimum 30 g, maximum 80 mL) emulsified in 100–150 mL water, administered as a single dose via the routinely placed nasogastric tube after induction of general anesthesia and endotracheal intubation.

Control group: Patients receive standard perioperative care without administration of a fatty acid emulsion. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned elective major pancreatic resection (partial pancreatoduodenectomy, or total pancreatectomy) for any indication
Age ≥ 18 years
ASA classification ≤ III
Ability of the patient to understand the nature and individual consequences of the clinical trial
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Known clinically relevant allergy to long-chain fatty acids or vegetable oils
Participation in another interventional trial with interference of the intervention and/or outcomes of this study
Intraoperative findings or decisions precluding performance of the trial intervention (e.g. unexpected technical or anatomical conditions; reasons will be documented)
